title: WPMS/2040/2018 of Suresh Kumar Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2040 of 2018

Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö.ÖRespondents
Present:- Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate, for the petitioner.
 Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate General, for the State/respondent
nos.1 & 2.
 Ms. Monika Pant, Central Government Standing Counsel, for the Union
of India/respondent nos.3 & 4.

Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 The petitioner before this Court is a Post
Master in the Postal Department. During his service, there
were certain charges of embezzlement against the petitioner
and the petitioner was dismissed from service as long back
as in the year 2001. Thereafter, the recovery certificate was
issued against the petitioner on 15.05.2013, which was to
the tune of Rs.2,13,162/- (Rupees Two Lakh Thirteen
Thousand One Hundred Sixty Two Only). Against which,
the petitioner had preferred a writ petition before this Court
being WPMS No.1523 of 2013, in which the following order
was passed by this Court:-
ìMr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. B.S. Parihar, Standing Counsel for the State.
Learned counsel for the petitioner prays for and
is permitted to withdraw this petition.
The writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn with
liberty reserved to the petitioner to file fresh
petition within three months, in view of
subsequent development.
Till then, no recovery shall be effected from the
petitioner.î

2
2. The petitioner has now preferred the present
writ petition after a gap of more than six months wherein
he again challenged the recovery certificate dated
15.05.2013 which he had challenged in the first writ
petition, which was already dismissed as withdrawn vide
order dated 08.12.2017. Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that the petitioner was never conveyed the
termination order and against which the petitioner has
already preferred a departmental appeal in March 2018
before the concerned authority, which is still pending.

3. Considering the overall facts and
circumstances of the case, this Court is not inclined to
interfere in the matter.
4. In view thereof, the writ petition stands
dismissed in limine.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 18.07.2018
Nitesh/
